It is known that A corresponds to the straight line in the figure, and B corresponds to the curve in the figure. Then what motion does B undergo?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a graph of the position coordinate x changing with time t, with the vertical axis as x and the horizontal axis as t. There is a straight line and an upward-curving curve in the figure; the stem states that A corresponds to the straight line and B corresponds to the curve. B's curve is not a straight line, and it curves upward with time; the slope at each point of the curve is changing. Reasoning: In an x-t graph, the slope of the graph line represents the object's velocity. The slope of the curve corresponding to B changes with time, indicating that the magnitude of B's velocity is changing. Also, because the stem states that both A and B move on the same straight line, B's trajectory of motion is a straight line. Therefore B undergoes variable-speed rectilinear motion. Final answer: B undergoes variable-speed rectilinear motion.
